text.p: - General Alexander Lebed may be easy to evict from power but not from the Russian political arena where "tough guys" are in demand.
- "We are used to all this 'settling of accounts' they have in Moscow and ignore them," Viktor Chechevatov, commander of the Far Eastern military district, says in reference to Lebed's sacking.
- Cinema halls, once immensely popular with Muscovites, have fallen on hard times and many of them could soon be turned into shops and cafeterias.
- The situation in Chechnya could be fraught with most unpredictable consequences after General Lebed's sacking on Thursday.
- Most Russian banks need help from the Central Bank and it is likely that political considerations will play a major role in deciding their fate.
- Dangerous tax shortfalls have made the government speak of a possible change of economic course for the first time in five years.
- General Lebed's sacking will certainly calm down passions in Moscow but the Kremlin could be in for a spot of bother from Chechnya.
- Professional politicians are those who know how to "digest" differences of opinion internally and not break them into the open.
- General Lebed and Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov made Russia blush when they let the bitter political infighting go completely public.
